To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“The Hartley Phase Spectra (HPS) of speech and audio signals, which are extracted via the Hartly Transform and are free of phase discontinuites, are a promising feature for classification.”.
the Hartley Phase spectrum is an effective assistive feature for classification of speech and audio signals.

the Hartley Phase spectrum is a useful tool for classification, when the magnitude content is not sufficient to achieve the desired classification rate, as is the case in certain speech and audio classification tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the phase spectrum of a signal as a source of information for feature extraction and its use as a complementary feature to the magnitude spectrum of a signal.
the development of a novel phase extraction method for speech and audio classification and the evaluation of the performance of the proposed method in the context of audio classification.
the following questions: (i) Can the phase spectrum be used as an assistive feature for classification?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of magnitude and phase features, extracted from the Hartley Phase spectrum, improves the classification rate for certain audio classes.
the Hartley Phase spectrum is a useful tool to assist in the classification of audio classes where the magnitude content of a signal underperforms in classification.
the phase of a signal is a valuable feature for speech recognition and audio classification and that the Hartley Phase spectrum is a reliable tool for extracting the phase information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed method is capable of improving the classification rate of a classifier, in the case where the magnitude content of a class underperforms in comparison to the case where the phase content of a class is used.
the proposed approach is able to increase the recognition rate of a classifier when the magnitude content underperformed in terms of recognition.
the Hartley Phase spectrum can be used as an additional feature to the magnitude spectrum for speech and audio classification.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Hartley Phase spectrum is a promising alternative to the standard Fourier Phase for feature extraction in speech recognition tasks.

phase related features can be successfully combined with magnitude features in order to enhance the classification rate of certain audio and speech classes, while the proposed Hartley Phase Spectrum is a reliable tool for phase extraction.
the Hartley Phase is a valuable feature for classification, especially for those cases where the phase content of a signal is not captured by its magnitude spectrum.
